text: {"features":[{"name":"Security mission motivation","description":"How convincingly the letter explains why the applicant wants to work in security engineering rather than in a generic software role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives little or no reason for wanting security work specifically, beyond generic impact, prestige, or interest in software engineering."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"States a general interest in security impact, but the rationale remains broad, conventional, or lightly developed."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides a clear reason security appeals, such as prevention, resilience, or reducing incidents, but keeps the motivation mostly general."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Articulates a thoughtful security philosophy that is tied to prior experience or to a clearly stated way of working."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes security motivation feel central and credible by linking a distinctive worldview about prevention, attacker thinking, or quiet resilience to past work and future contribution."}]},{"name":"Role targeting","description":"How specifically the letter connects the applicant's background to this exact Google Information Security Engineering role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Could plausibly be sent to many backend or security roles, with little connection to this team's stated work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Names the team or title but discusses fit in mostly generic terms without engaging the core responsibilities."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Connects the applicant to one or two major elements of the posting, such as secure development lifecycle work or security automation."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Tailors the letter to several specific responsibilities, such as vulnerability handling, AI agents, developer enablement, or collaboration with security engineers."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Feels written for this exact role by explicitly linking the applicant's experience to the team's mandate, technical stack, and Google-wide security leverage."}]},{"name":"Platform enablement mindset","description":"How strongly the letter shows an orientation toward building secure defaults, reducing friction, and enabling other engineers at scale.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Focuses mostly on personal growth or generic impact, with little sense of helping other engineers work more securely."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions scale or broad impact, but not how security tooling should serve developers or reduce friction."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows some appreciation for foundational or organization-wide tooling, though the developer-enablement angle is limited."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clearly emphasizes secure defaults, workload reduction, or systems that help product teams do the right thing more easily."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Consistently frames security engineering as an enablement problem, highlighting leverage, low-friction workflows, and durable improvements inherited across many teams."}]},{"name":"Formal technical preparation","description":"How strong the letter's formal academic preparation is for advanced software and security engineering work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Presents only the baseline minimum of a bachelor's degree, with no suggestion of graduate-level formal training."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows slightly stronger formal preparation than the baseline through additional technical study or equivalent framing, but not a completed graduate degree."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents a master's degree in computer science or a closely related technical field."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents doctoral-level study or another clearly advanced graduate background, though the added depth is only lightly connected to the role."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Uses advanced graduate training as a major strength for the application, typically a doctorate clearly reinforcing readiness for complex security engineering work."}]},{"name":"Production systems experience","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates professional experience testing, maintaining, and launching production software systems relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Describes only modest professional scope, around the low end of the sample in years and number of production services."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows basic production experience but with either limited tenure or limited variety of launch and maintenance responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives solid hands-on evidence of maintaining and launching several services or spending about five years in production engineering."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial repeated ownership across multiple production services over several years, covering testing, maintenance, and launch."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Conveys extensive production experience at the top of the sample range, pairing long tenure with broad responsibility for many services across the full lifecycle."}]},{"name":"Go expertise","description":"How convincingly the letter presents the applicant as ready to design and implement Go back-end systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mentions Go only as one of several languages, with no sign of meaningful use or ownership."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows some professional Go use, but not enough detail to judge depth or backend responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Presents Go as a regular production language and links it to launched or maintained services."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Frames Go as a main or daily language behind backend or infrastructure work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows strong role-ready Go depth by positioning Go as the primary language for designing and implementing production back ends or agent infrastructure."}]},{"name":"Python expertise","description":"How convincingly the letter shows production-ready Python use relevant to automation and AI agents.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention Python, or mentions it only indirectly without any evidence of use."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions occasional Python use with little detail about what it is used for or how substantial it is."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States regular Python use for tooling, scripts, services, or prototypes in production work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial Python responsibility across services and internal automation, making Python clearly relevant to the role."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents Python as production-grade and central, supported by concrete evidence such as typed or tested services, internal platforms, or agent implementations."}]},{"name":"AI production experience","description":"How well the letter demonstrates hands-on work with AI systems in production settings.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of AI experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI interest or light exposure, but gives no clear sign of shipped work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Notes building or shipping AI or LLM features, but with limited detail about context, responsibility, or operating constraints."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes production AI work with some attention to reliability, trustworthiness, or evaluation."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows substantial, role-relevant AI experience by pairing shipped model-backed features with concrete discussion of guardrails, evaluation, or trustworthy operation."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems design","description":"How strongly the letter demonstrates design of agentic tooling or autonomous workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of agentic systems experience."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"References agents only abstractly or as a future interest, without showing direct design work."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Claims end-to-end agent or pipeline design, but gives only limited architecture detail."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explains a clear agent architecture, typically separating Python agents from service infrastructure or operational constraints."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents agentic design as deliberate engineering, with bounded actions, contracts, permissions, auditing, or guardrails tied to Go back ends and Python agents."}]},{"name":"Security assessment capability","description":"How well the letter evidences the ability to assess systems for security risk.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of security assessment work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Implies general security awareness, but does not show concrete assessment activity."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States experience with security assessments or reviews in general terms, without much detail about method or scope."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or remediation follow-through."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows strong assessment practice by leading or repeatedly performing structured reviews across services and validating fixes with an attacker-minded approach."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability response automation","description":"How directly the letter demonstrates building automation for vulnerability intake, triage, routing, or related response workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of vulnerability-handling work or relevant automation."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses interest in reducing security toil, but gives no direct example of doing so."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Mentions some automation of vulnerability reports or triage, with limited detail about the workflow or impact."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes building a concrete pipeline for classification, deduplication, prioritization, or routing of vulnerability reports."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows especially strong fit by presenting vulnerability automation as owned work with clear operational impact, such as turning a manual queue into a largely self-serve system or multiplying expert capacity."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic strength","description":"How convincingly the letter shows practical command of data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of algorithmic or data-structure work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Makes a generic claim of enjoying algorithms or having strong fundamentals, without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives one concrete example of algorithmic improvement or hot-path redesign."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes substantial algorithmic work tied to system performance or correctness, such as graph algorithms, indexing, scheduling, matching, or deduplication."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents algorithmic ability as a clear strength with concrete examples showing principled redesign that materially improved a difficult or previously brittle system."}]},{"name":"External security validation","description":"How strong the letter's externally validated evidence is of security skill through certifications or competitive practice.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Offers no external validation of security ability."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows only a light outside signal of security interest, without a recognized credential or notable achievement."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Provides one baseline external signal, such as CompTIA Security+ or routine competitive practice without notable results."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Provides a strong external signal, such as OSCP or serious competitive security involvement with credible placements."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Combines multiple strong external signals, such as OSCP alongside high-level competitive results or similarly rigorous outside validation."}]},{"name":"Open-source stewardship","description":"How much the letter demonstrates contribution to or maintenance of open-source software.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of open-source involvement."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions only very light open-source interaction, without contribution or ownership."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Notes occasional patches or upstream fixes to dependencies."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Describes maintaining or regularly contributing to an open-source project with some responsibility for review or releases."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows substantial open-source stewardship, such as maintaining an actively used project or framework with external users, ongoing contribution review, and release ownership."}]},{"name":"Personal project sophistication","description":"How much the letter uses personal technical projects to demonstrate engineering depth.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no personal project, or only a very slight hobby mention with no technical substance."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small side project mainly as a sign of curiosity, with limited technical complexity."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes a useful personal project with some nontrivial engineering choices or implementation detail."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents a substantial project involving meaningful systems concerns such as replication, failover, compaction, consensus, or recovery."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Uses a sustained, technically ambitious project to demonstrate deep systems skill through hard distributed-systems or infrastructure problems and clear lessons learned."}]},{"name":"Specificity of evidence","description":"How concrete and observable the letter's claims are, including examples, responsibilities, and outcomes.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mostly on generic assertions, with little concrete support for the applicant's claims."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes a few specifics, but leaves many important claims unsubstantiated or vague."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Supports several claims with concrete examples, though impact, scope, or outcomes remain somewhat general."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently grounds claims in specific responsibilities, technologies, or before-and-after improvements."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Makes nearly every major claim tangible through precise examples, scope, and observable results, creating strong credibility without unnecessary padding."}]},{"name":"Organization","description":"How clearly the letter is structured and how smoothly ideas progress from one point to the next.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Feels fragmented or hard to follow, with abrupt jumps, list-like fragments, or weak progression."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has a recognizable structure, but sequencing is uneven and transitions are choppy."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Reads clearly overall, though some sections feel loosely connected or mechanically assembled."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Moves logically through motivation, qualifications, and evidence with mostly smooth transitions."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is especially well-composed, with a deliberate progression that makes the case easy to follow and cumulative in effect."}]},{"name":"Writing mechanics","description":"How polished the prose is at the level of spelling, grammar, and copyediting.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Contains frequent mechanical errors that are distracting and call attention to lack of care."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has multiple noticeable spelling or grammar errors that interrupt reading but do not obscure meaning."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Has a few visible mechanical errors, yet remains generally professional and readable."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Is nearly error-free, with only isolated minor slips."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is clean and polished throughout, with no noticeable mechanical issues."}]}]}
